item.title: Re: CHALLENGE: MrWrong's Fill Up the SCP Map Challenge
item.content:encoded:
Looking at the sites, I can get a few locations.

-Site-15, seeing on how it studies electronics and computing, could theoretically be in Silicon Valley. The description only says California, however.
-Site 77 is in Southern Italy
-Site 88 is in Baldwin County, Alabama.
-Site 64 is in Forest Park, near Portland, Oregon.

Anyways, maybe I can cook up something for one of these areas.

item.title: Re: CHALLENGE: MrWrong's Fill Up the SCP Map Challenge
item.content:encoded:
Hm, in the map, there's only one SCP from Vietnam, SCP-1973. But the article says that the anomaly documented is located in USA with Vietnam as one of the possible entrances/exits. Does it count as a Vietnamese SCP? If not, I'd like to join this challenge and write one for it.

Frankly, the map thing is just an arbitrary starting point. If you have an idea and you want to write about it, no one can really stop you.

Oh wait, does Object-0401-42 count? That girl who caused the Chernobyl Disaster? She is contained by GRU-P Division, and neutralized before the Foundation got their hands on her, so does she count as an SCP?

I am counting only things that are explicitly SCP articles.

item.title: Re: MrWrong's Fill Up the SCP Map Challenge

item.title: Re: MrWrong's Fill Up the SCP Map Challenge
item.content:encoded:
make an SCP found/manifested in a country/dependency/state/province/sub-national division that has no SCPs on the map above.

By all means, go ahead. The South Island can't be void of anomalies.

As for Antarctica, since there are SCPs on the landmass itself, any more won't count towards the challenge (but feel free to put more). It's mainly due to the fact that Antarctica is strictly speaking terra nullius.

item.title: MrWrong's Fill Up the SCP Map Challenge
item.content:encoded:
https://www.zeemaps.com/map?group=1296235

Thanks to Guilliman, SCPs are mapped according to where they're found. Yet there're many countries not filled up (North American and Western Europe are practically saturated with SCPs).

Your challenge, should you choose to accept, is to make an SCP found/manifested in a country/dependency/state/province/sub-national division that has no SCPs on the map above. Pick your chosen area and start writing about what kind of SCP can the Foundation find in these "frontiers".
